title: Buck Clayton's lip operation and drinking
summary: Edison says doctors cut a muscle in Clayton's lip unnecessarily, and he understands a musician drinking after losing his playing.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: But Buck doesn't -- Buck seems to , I don't know what it is with him, whether it's mental or what?

No, you know, they operated on his lip one time. And they cut a little muscle there, right in his embouchure. And had the doctor looked -- examined his teeth, he would have found out what was keeping his lip sore was a little hang-down on his tooth, just file it down. And after he had operated on his lip and cut this little muscle, then he found out that all he had to have done was to just file his tooth down.
Oh, yeah. It was a horrible thing that happened to Buck. He never should really have -- well, it was the doctor's fault, really.
I didn't know that. I knew that Buck was always very nice about it and I knew there was something wrong.
Oh, yeah. He really should have -- well, the doctor should never have done anything to his lip.
Oh, that's terrible. But still, look what you did to your teeth, busted for nothing.

Yeah, this dentist just broke it off, you know. But I think Buck is to be commended, you know, not to play for seven years and then keep trying, keep trying, you know. He's improving everyday now that he's playing.
Of course, the thing is he's got to play, doesn't he. Otherwise --
Well, he's a good writer. Oh, he can write. Thank God, he could write, you know. Otherwise, he would have been in trouble.
Yeah, but the only thing -- you know, I know two or three years ago when he was starting and everything, he would get discouraged and then he'd drink too much. So the two things can go together.
Yeah. Well, I can understand him drinking, too. I can understand it. Because when you've lost, you

know, the thing that really is responsible for your existence, you know, and that's only the thing you've done -- see, musicians can't do -- most of them can't do anything but what they've done because you devote all your life to your profession. You devote your -- all your life to improve your style. You constantly have to think of something different to play, something that's going to make the evening pleasant to the people you're playing to. You're constantly worrying about are you really accomplishing anything, you know.
It's quite a task to wake up every morning and have to play every night. And all day you're thinking, what am I going to play tonight, you know.
